desc:
A non-decreasing array (repeated values allowed) was cut at some position into a front part and a back part and the two parts were swapped, producing nums. For example [4, 5, 1, 2, 4, 4] comes from [1, 2, 4, 4, 4, 5]: a value can now appear at both ends of the array.

Return the smallest index i such that nums[i] == target, or -1 if there is none. For nums = [4, 5, 1, 2, 4, 4] and target = 4 the answer is 0 (not 4), for target = 2 it is 3, and for target = 3 it is -1. Aim for O(log n) on typical inputs.
constraints: nums is a rotation of a non-decreasing array
hints: Equal values can be split between the front and the back of the array, so finding 'a' match is not enough. First you need a reliable anchor: where does the sorted order start?

Find the start index s of the sorted order. If nums[mid] == nums[hi], check whether nums[hi - 1] > nums[hi] (then hi is the start); otherwise drop hi. Then the virtual array nums[(s + j) % n] is sorted, and a lower-bound and an upper-bound search give the block of equal values.

That block occupies virtual positions [a, b). Virtual position j lives at real index s + j if that is below n, otherwise at s + j - n. Any copy that wrapped around has a smaller real index than every copy that did not, so prefer the first wrapped position max(a, n - s) when it is inside the block.
editorial: Step 1: locate the start s of the sorted order, the unique index whose left neighbour is larger (or 0 if the array is sorted). Binary search with window [lo, hi]: a larger nums[mid] than nums[hi] moves lo to mid + 1, a smaller one moves hi to mid, and a tie is resolved by returning hi if nums[hi - 1] > nums[hi] and otherwise dropping hi. This is O(log n) typically and O(n) in the worst case, which cannot be avoided with duplicates.

Step 2: in the virtual sorted array v[j] = nums[(s + j) % n] binary search the first position a with v[a] ≥ target and the first position b with v[b] > target. If a == b the target is absent: return -1.

Step 3: translate back. Positions j < n - s map to real index s + j (these are at or after s), positions j ≥ n - s map to s + j - n (these are before s, hence smaller). So if the block reaches the wrapped region (b - 1 ≥ n - s) the answer is s + max(a, n - s) - n; otherwise it is s + a. Space O(1).
